memory_candidates.content: An flock belongs to the open file description, so a child process that re-opens a lock file its parent already holds is excluded by that parent and waits out its full timeout. Take a shared advisory lock only in the leaf script that performs the guarded operation, never in a delegating caller, and place it after every build-free early exit. For hours-long runners, open the lock fd inside a subshell around just the build step so the lock is released when the subshell exits.

To verify lock, timeout and post-acquisition control flow in a script that shells out to a build tool without running the tool: put a stub executable of the same name first on PATH (logs its argv, exits with an env-chosen status, optionally prints a chosen stderr line), and hold the lock from a second process with a bounded 'flock FILE sleep N'. Size N above the runtime of the command under test, or the holder expires before the branch is reached.
